questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the sex ratio in Census 2011:
1. Kerala has the highest sex ratio among the States.
2. Haryana has the lowest sex ratio among the States.
3. Puducherry has the highest sex ratio among all States and Union Territories.
questions.e: Kerala (1084) is the highest and Haryana (879) the lowest among States. Puducherry (1037) is the highest among Union Territories but still below Kerala, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q: Which one of the following States recorded the lowest literacy rate (7+ years) in Census 2011?
questions.e: Bihar had the lowest literacy rate among States in 2011 (about 63.8 percent), against the national figure of about 74 percent. Arunachal Pradesh, Rajasthan and Jharkhand were also below average but higher than Bihar.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about population density in Census 2011:
1. The density of population for India was 382 persons per sq km.
2. Bihar had the highest density among the States.
3. Sikkim had the lowest density among the States.
4. Delhi had the highest density among all States and Union Territories.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: India's density was 382 and Bihar (1106) topped the States, while Delhi (11,297) was the densest of all. The lowest density among States was Arunachal Pradesh (17), not Sikkim (86), so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q: A country where the death rate has begun to fall because of better medicine and sanitation, while the birth rate remains high, is passing through which stage of the demographic transition?
questions.e: In stage 2 death rates fall first (health care, food supply) but birth rates stay high from habit and social norms, so population grows fast. In stage 1 both rates are high, in stage 3 the birth rate also falls, and in stage 4 both are low.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 2
questions.h: Death falls first, births follow later

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about urbanisation in Census 2011:
1. Goa was the most urbanised State.
2. Kerala was the most urbanised State.
3. About 31 percent of India's population lived in urban areas.
questions.e: Goa (62.17 percent urban) was the most urbanised State; Kerala's share was well below Goa's, so statement 2 is wrong. The national urban share was 31.16 percent.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following criteria used in Census 2011 to identify a Census Town:
1. A minimum population of 5,000.
2. At least 75 percent of the male main working population engaged in non-agricultural pursuits.
3. A density of population of at least 400 persons per sq km.
4. Places with a municipality, corporation or cantonment board are called statutory towns, a separate category from Census Towns.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three numeric conditions must be met together for a Census Town. Places with a legally notified local body (municipality, corporation, cantonment board, notified area committee) are statutory towns, so statement 4 is also correct.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q: Which one of the following sovereign countries has the lowest population density in the world?
questions.e: Mongolia, a vast landlocked country of steppe and desert with a small population, has about 2 persons per sq km. Namibia, Australia and Iceland are also very sparsely settled but have slightly higher densities. Greenland is lower still but is not a sovereign country.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about age composition and dependency:
1. The dependency ratio is the ratio of the working-age population to the dependent population.
2. In the NCERT/Census classification, dependants are children below 15 years and persons above 59 years.
3. A large share of the population in the working ages can yield a demographic dividend if productively employed.
questions.e: The dependency ratio compares dependants (young and old) with the working-age group, so statement 1 states it upside down. A bulge in working ages raises output per head, which is the demographic dividend.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Population Policy, 2000:
1. Its medium-term objective was to bring the Total Fertility Rate to replacement levels by 2010.
2. Its long-term objective was to achieve a stable population by 2045.
3. It set a target of reaching a zero population growth rate by 2025.
questions.e: The policy aimed at replacement-level TFR by 2010 and a stable population by 2045, consistent with sustainable development. It set no target of zero growth by 2025.
questions.s: National Population Policy 2000, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Family Health Survey-5 (2019-21):
1. India's Total Fertility Rate was around 2.0, below the replacement level.
2. Every State had a Total Fertility Rate below the replacement level.
3. The replacement level fertility is taken as 2.1 children per woman.
questions.e: NFHS-5 put India's TFR near 2.0, below the 2.1 needed to replace a population. The national average hides variation: a few States such as Bihar and Meghalaya remained above 2.1, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: NFHS-5 national report, MoHFW

questions.q:
Statement-I: The population pyramid of Japan has a narrow base and a broad top.
Statement-II: Japan has a very low birth rate combined with a high life expectancy, which gives it a large share of elderly people.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Few births shrink the youngest age groups, while long lives swell the oldest ones, giving a contracting (declining) pyramid. Statement-II therefore directly explains Statement-I.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 2

questions.q:
Match List-I (Thinker) with List-II (Idea) and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I
A. Malthus
B. Edwin Cannan
C. Warren Thompson
List-II
1. Optimum population
2. Demographic transition
3. Population grows geometrically while food supply grows arithmetically
questions.e: Malthus linked growth to food supply in his essay of 1798, Cannan developed the optimum population concept, and Thompson (later extended by Notestein) outlined the demographic transition model.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 2; Majid Husain
questions.h: Malthus = Math, Cannan = Count the best, Thompson = Transition

questions.q:
Arrange the following States in descending order of population as per Census 2011:
1. Bihar
2. Maharashtra
3. Uttar Pradesh
4. West Bengal
questions.e: Uttar Pradesh (about 19.98 crore) was first, Maharashtra (about 11.24 crore) second, Bihar (about 10.41 crore) third and West Bengal (about 9.13 crore) fourth.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q: Which one of the following was the only State in India to record a negative decadal population growth between 2001 and 2011?
questions.e: Nagaland's population fell by about 0.58 percent in the decade, the only State with a negative growth rate. Kerala and Goa had low but positive growth, while Manipur grew by about a quarter.
questions.s: Census of India 2011; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about road corridors in India:
1. The Golden Quadrilateral links Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata.
2. The North-South corridor runs from Srinagar to Kanyakumari.
3. The East-West corridor runs from Porbandar to Silchar.
4. The Golden Quadrilateral includes Bengaluru as one of its four corner cities.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The Golden Quadrilateral joins the four metros; Bengaluru is not a corner, so statement 4 is wrong. The NS and EW corridors under NHDP cross the country diagonally along the stated routes.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 10

questions.q:
Match List-I (Railway Zone) with List-II (Headquarters):
List-I
A. Northeast Frontier
B. East Coast
C. West Central
D. East Central
List-II
1. Hajipur
2. Jabalpur
3. Bhubaneswar
4. Maligaon
questions.e: Northeast Frontier Railway is headquartered at Maligaon (Guwahati), East Coast at Bhubaneswar, West Central at Jabalpur and East Central at Hajipur in Bihar.
questions.s: Indian Railways zonal list; Majid Husain

questions.q: The Konkan Railway, which passes through Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka, runs between which of the following?
questions.e: Konkan Railway runs along the west coast from Roha in Maharashtra to Thokur near Mangaluru in Karnataka, passing through Goa on the way. It was built through the difficult terrain between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 10

questions.q:
Match List-I (National Waterway) with List-II (Stretch):
List-I
A. NW-1
B. NW-2
C. NW-3
List-II
1. Sadiya to Dhubri on the Brahmaputra
2. Kollam to Kottapuram on the West Coast Canal
3. Prayagraj to Haldia on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly
questions.e: NW-1 follows the Ganga system from Prayagraj to Haldia, NW-2 the Brahmaputra from Sadiya to Dhubri, and NW-3 the Kerala backwater canal from Kollam to Kottapuram.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 10; IWAI
questions.h: NW-1 Ganga, NW-2 Assam, NW-3 Kerala

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian ports:
1. Paradip Port is located on the west coast.
2. Haldia dock complex was developed to relieve congestion at Kolkata port.
3. Jawaharlal Nehru Port was developed to decongest Mumbai port.
questions.e: Kolkata is a riverine port with silting problems, so Haldia was built downstream to share its traffic. Nhava Sheva (JNPT) was built across the harbour to ease Mumbai. Paradip is on the Odisha coast (east), so statement 1 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 10

questions.q: The Hazira-Bijaipur-Jagdishpur (HBJ) gas pipeline links which of the following sets of States?
o: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
questions.e: The HBJ pipeline carries gas from the western offshore fields via Hazira (Gujarat) through Bijaipur (Madhya Pradesh) to Jagdishpur (Uttar Pradesh), supplying fertiliser and power plants along the way.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 10
questions.h: Hazira, Bijaipur, Jagdishpur = Guj, MP, UP

questions.q:
Match List-I (Trans-continental Railway) with List-II (Route):
List-I
A. Trans-Siberian
B. Canadian Pacific
C. Trans-Australian
D. Orient Express
List-II
1. Montreal to Vancouver
2. Paris to Istanbul
3. Moscow to Vladivostok
4. Sydney to Perth
questions.e: The Trans-Siberian crosses Russia to the Pacific port of Vladivostok, the Canadian Pacific joins the St Lawrence region with the Pacific coast, and the Trans-Australian links east and west coasts across the Nullarbor.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 7

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about important canals:
1. The Suez Canal has no locks.
2. The Panama Canal uses a system of locks.
3. The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Persian Gulf.
4. The Kiel Canal connects the Baltic Sea with the Black Sea.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Suez is a sea-level canal as the two seas lie at nearly the same height, while Panama must raise ships over the isthmus through locks. Suez joins the Mediterranean with the Red Sea, and Kiel joins the North Sea with the Baltic.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 7

questions.q:
Statement-I: Water transport is the cheapest means of carrying bulky goods over long distances.
Statement-II: Water transport is the fastest mode of transport.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Water transport has low friction and large carrying capacity, so cost per tonne-km is low for bulk cargo such as ore, grain and oil. It is, however, slow compared with air, rail and road transport.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 7

questions.q:
Statement-I: Kandla is a tidal port.
Statement-II: Kandla was developed after Partition to make up for the loss of Karachi port.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Kandla on the Gulf of Kachchh depends on the tides for ship movement, and it was built after 1947 when Karachi went to Pakistan. The reason for its construction, however, does not explain its tidal character.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 10

questions.q:
Match List-I (Temperate Grassland) with List-II (Region):
List-I
A. Veld
B. Downs
C. Pampas
D. Steppe
List-II
1. Argentina and Uruguay
2. Australia
3. South Africa
4. Eurasia
questions.e: Veld belongs to South Africa, Downs to Australia (and New Zealand's Canterbury), Pampas to Argentina and Uruguay, and Steppe to Eurasia. Prairies are the North American equivalent.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about world production of plantation crops:
1. Colombia is the largest producer of coffee.
2. Vietnam is the second largest producer of coffee.
3. China is the largest producer of tea.
questions.e: Brazil, not Colombia, leads coffee production, and Vietnam (mostly robusta) is second. China produces the most tea, with India second.
questions.s: FAO / International Coffee Organization; NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 4

questions.q:
Match List-I (Crop) with List-II (Leading World Producer):
List-I
A. Cocoa
B. Oil palm
C. Natural rubber
D. Jute
List-II
1. Thailand
2. India
3. Cote d'Ivoire
4. Indonesia
questions.e: West Africa's humid forest belt makes Cote d'Ivoire the cocoa leader, Indonesia has overtaken Malaysia in palm oil, Thailand leads natural rubber and the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta region makes India the leading jute producer.
questions.s: FAO; NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 4

questions.q: Which one of the following regions does NOT have a Mediterranean type of climate and agriculture?
questions.e: Mediterranean regions lie on the western sides of continents between roughly 30 and 40 degrees latitude, with wet winters and dry summers. Southern Brazil is on the eastern side and has a humid subtropical climate with rain in all seasons.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about fishing:
1. The Grand Banks lie where the cold Labrador Current meets the warm Gulf Stream.
2. Dogger Bank is a fishing ground in the Baltic Sea.
3. Mixing of warm and cold currents reduces plankton and hence the fish catch.
4. Continental shelves are generally less productive than the deep ocean basins.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Mixing of currents brings nutrients and plankton to the surface, which attracts fish, and shallow shelves with sunlight reaching the bottom are the richest grounds. Dogger Bank is in the North Sea, so only statement 1 is correct.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about economic activities:
1. Retail trading is a quaternary activity.
2. Quaternary activities centre on the collection, production and dissemination of information.
3. Quinary activities involve the highest level of decision making, as done by senior executives and policy makers.
questions.e: Retail trade is a tertiary service. Quaternary activities deal with knowledge and information, and quinary activities are the top-level decision-making layer.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 6

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the World Trade Organization (WTO):
1. It came into being in 1995 as the successor to the GATT.
2. Its headquarters are at Geneva.
3. It is a specialised agency of the United Nations.
questions.e: WTO replaced the GATT system on 1 January 1995 after the Uruguay Round and sits at Geneva. It is an independent organisation, not a UN specialised agency.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 8

questions.q:
Statement-I: Chile is a founding member of Mercosur.
Statement-II: Mercosur was established by the Treaty of Asuncion in 1991.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The founders were Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, who signed the Treaty of Asuncion in 1991. Chile joined later only as an associate state, so Statement-I is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 8

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kandla Free Trade Zone, set up in 1965, was the first zone of its kind in India.
2. The Santacruz Electronics Export Processing Zone (SEEPZ) at Mumbai was India's first export processing zone.
3. The Special Economic Zones Act was enacted in 2005.
questions.e: Kandla in Gujarat (1965) pre-dates SEEPZ, which was set up in the 1970s, so statement 2 is wrong. The SEZ Act of 2005 replaced the earlier export processing zone scheme.
questions.s: Ministry of Commerce, SEZ policy; NCERT Class XII India People and Economy Ch 1 (International Trade chapter)

questions.q:
Match List-I (Shifting Cultivation Name) with List-II (Region):
List-I
A. Milpa
B. Roca
C. Ladang
D. Masole
List-II
1. Indonesia and Malaysia
2. Central Africa
3. Central America and Mexico
4. Brazil
questions.e: The same slash-and-burn system has local names: milpa in Mexico and Central America, roca in Brazil, ladang in Malaysia and Indonesia, masole in Central Africa, and jhum in north-east India.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 4
questions.h: Jhum in India, Milpa in Mexico

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Term : Meaning
1. Fazenda : Coffee estate in Brazil
2. Estancia : Large cattle or sheep ranch in Argentina
3. Kolkhoz : Collective farm in the former USSR
4. Sovkhoz : Collective farm in the former USSR
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: A sovkhoz was a state-owned farm worked by wage labour, whereas a kolkhoz was the collective farm in which members pooled land and equipment. The other three pairs are correct.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 4

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of pastoral nomadic community and region is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: The Tuareg are camel-herding people of the Sahara. Reindeer herders of Scandinavia are the Sami (Lapps).
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 4

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a community that practises transhumance in the Himalaya?
questions.e: Gaddis, Bakarwals and Bhotias move herds seasonally between high summer pastures and lower winter valleys. The Todas are buffalo-herders of the Nilgiri hills in the south.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about trade:
1. Balance of trade records the difference between the value of exports and imports of goods.
2. Balance of payments is a broader record that also includes services, transfers and capital flows.
3. A surplus in the balance of trade always means a surplus in the balance of payments.
questions.e: The trade balance covers merchandise only, while the balance of payments adds services, transfers and capital flows. A trade surplus can be offset by a capital outflow, so a payments surplus is not guaranteed.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography Ch 8

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Survey of India topographical sheets:
1. A 1:250,000 sheet covers an area of 1 degree by 1 degree.
2. Each 1:250,000 sheet is divided into 16 sheets at 1:50,000.
3. A 1:50,000 sheet covers 30 minutes by 30 minutes.
questions.e: One degree is four times 15 minutes, so a 1x1 degree sheet splits into 4x4 = 16 sheets of 15' x 15' at 1:50,000. A 1:50,000 sheet therefore covers 15', not 30'.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Practical Work in Geography (Topographical Maps)

questions.q: On a map with a representative fraction of 1:50,000, two places are 8 cm apart. The actual distance between them is
questions.e: At 1:50,000, 1 cm on the map is 50,000 cm = 500 m on the ground. Eight centimetres therefore equal 4,000 m = 4 km.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Practical Work in Geography (Maps and Scale)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about contours:
1. Closely spaced contours indicate a steep slope.
2. Contours of different elevations cross each other on a gentle slope.
3. Closed concentric contours with higher values inside represent a hill.
4. In a river valley the V-shapes of the contours point downstream.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Steep slopes compress the vertical interval into a small horizontal distance, and rising values inward mean a hill. Contours of different heights do not cross except at a cliff or overhang, and in a valley the V points upstream towards higher ground.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Practical Work in Geography (Topographical Maps)

questions.q: When it is 12 noon at 75 degrees East, the local time at 15 degrees West is
questions.e: The difference in longitude is 90 degrees and the Earth turns 15 degrees per hour, a gap of 6 hours. Places to the west are behind in time, so it is 6:00 a.m.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography / Practical Work in Geography (Latitude, Longitude and Time)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Date Line:
1. It follows the 180 degree meridian exactly throughout its length.
2. It is deflected so that island groups such as Fiji and Tonga keep the same date.
3. A traveller crossing it from west to east sets the calendar back by one day.
questions.e: The line bends away from 180 degrees to avoid splitting island groups and countries into two dates. Moving eastward the date repeats, going back one day, and moving westward a day is skipped.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Practical Work in Geography (Time)

questions.q: Which one of the following States is NOT crossed by the Tropic of Cancer in India?
questions.e: The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight States: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha lies to the south of it.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India Physical Environment Ch 1

questions.q:
The Tropic of Capricorn passes through which of the following African countries?
1. Namibia
2. Botswana
3. Zimbabwe
4. Mozambique
How many of the above are crossed by it?
questions.e: At about 23.5 degrees south the line crosses Namibia, Botswana, South Africa, Mozambique and Madagascar. Zimbabwe lies wholly north of it.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography

questions.q: Which one of the following countries is NOT crossed by the Prime Meridian?
questions.e: The 0 degree meridian runs through the United Kingdom, France, Spain, Algeria, Mali, Burkina Faso, Togo and Ghana. Nigeria lies entirely east of it.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Practical Work in Geography

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Mercator projection is widely used for navigation charts.
Statement-II: On a Mercator map, a line of constant compass bearing appears as a straight line.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A navigator can steer a fixed compass course along a straight line drawn on the chart, which is why sailors favour this cylindrical projection despite its large area distortion near the poles.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Practical Work in Geography (Map Projections)

questions.q: On which one of the following projections do all great circles appear as straight lines?
questions.e: The gnomonic projection is drawn from the centre of the globe, so any great circle becomes a straight line, which makes it useful for plotting shortest routes. The other three do not have this property.
questions.s: Certificate Physical Geography (GC Leong); NCERT Class XI Practical Work

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of strait and the water bodies it connects is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bering Strait : Asia and North America
Strait of Gibraltar : Spain and Morocco
Strait of Hormuz : Saudi Arabia and Iran
Bab-el-Mandeb : Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
questions.e: Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and lies between Iran and Oman/UAE, not Saudi Arabia. The other pairs are correct.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography; Certificate Physical Geography

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about relief representation on maps:
1. A bench mark is a permanent surveyed point whose height is accurately marked on the map.
2. Layer tinting uses colour shades to show different altitude bands.
3. In hachures, steeper slopes are shown by longer and thinner lines.
questions.e: Bench marks and spot heights give exact elevations and tints show bands of altitude. In hachures, steeper slopes are drawn with shorter, thicker and closer lines, so statement 3 is reversed.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Practical Work in Geography (Maps)
